methodological_rigor.justification: CADENZA (NCT03386513) is an international phase I/II, open-label, single-arm, multicenter study in an ultrarare disease (BPDCN), appropriately using a 3+3 dose escalation followed by protocol-defined dose expansion in prespecified cohorts (PAP n=20 frontline de novo, overall frontline n=33, relapsed/refractory n=51). Sample sizes were prespecified to rule out reference rates (10% frontline, 5% relapsed/refractory) using two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson CIs; the manuscript explicitly states that interim analyses were not conducted and that 95% CIs were not adjusted for multiplicity. Investigator-assessed responses using prespecified CR/CRc criteria based on the tagraxofusp trial with CRh addition. Limitations include open-label single-arm design with no randomized comparator, reliance on investigator-assessed response, and protocol amendment to define the PAP de novo population (the authors transparently explain this).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Open-label single-arm phase I/II case-series in an ultrarare disease (Oxford 4). The clinical relevance is very high: CR+CRc 75% in frontline de novo BPDCN with median DOR 10.6 months and median OS 16.6 months, 53% of responders bridged to SCT, meaningful activity (14% CR+CRc) even in tagraxofusp-exposed relapsed/refractory disease, no CLS events, and convenient outpatient q3-week 30-minute infusion. The findings compare favorably to tagraxofusp, the only approved agent, and authors explicitly state the data support regulatory submission. For an ultrarare aggressive hematologic malignancy where randomized trials are infeasible, this represents a potentially practice-changing contribution.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript provides NCT03386513 registration, detailed patient disposition figure (Fig 1), eligibility criteria, prespecified primary and secondary endpoints, statistical analysis including Clopper-Pearson CIs and Kaplan-Meier censoring rules, and transparent disclosure of the protocol amendment defining the PAP. A representativeness table and subgroup analyses are provided. Funding and sponsor role (ImmunoGen/AbbVie designed the study and performed data collection and analysis) are explicitly disclosed. Data availability statement is not visible in the main text, and substantial detail is deferred to the Data Supplement.

novelty_literature.justification: Pivekimab sunirine is positioned as a first-in-class CD123 antibody-drug conjugate with an indolinobenzodiazepine pseudodimer payload that alkylates DNA via single-strand breaks, offering a novel mechanism compared to the approved CD123-directed cytotoxin tagraxofusp. Demonstrating meaningful activity in tagraxofusp-exposed relapsed/refractory BPDCN (previously reported preclinically to involve diphthamide-pathway resistance independent of CD123) is a conceptually novel clinical finding. The contribution is meaningful for an orphan disease though is confirmation within an established CD123 targeting strategy.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with clear sections on design, patients, efficacy by cohort, and safety with granular reporting of peripheral edema onset, VOD cases, and SCT bridging. Figure 1 (disposition), Figure 2 (OS by group), and Tables 1-3 communicate key data. The discussion appropriately situates findings against tagraxofusp (pivotal and long-term data), addresses VOD risk, and acknowledges small-sample limitations of exploratory SCT analyses.

key_strengths: High and durable response rates in frontline de novo BPDCN (CR+CRc 75%; median DOR 10.6 months; median OS 16.6 months) in an ultrarare aggressive disease
Meaningful activity in relapsed/refractory disease including tagraxofusp-exposed patients (57% of R/R cohort)
Convenient outpatient q3-week 30-minute infusion with no capillary leak syndrome events, an important tolerability advantage over tagraxofusp
Prespecified null hypotheses (10% frontline, 5% R/R) rejected; representativeness table and subgroup analyses provided
Directly supports regulatory submission in a rare indication where randomized trials are infeasible
key_concerns: Open-label single-arm design with no randomized comparator and investigator-assessed responses
Protocol amendment mid-study to define the de novo PAP population (transparently reported but reduces pre-specification strength)
Two on-treatment VOD cases and five post-SCT VOD cases require clearer risk stratification guidance
Sponsor (ImmunoGen/AbbVie) designed the study and performed data collection and analysis
No explicit data/code availability statement in the main text
chief_reviewer.rationale: A practice-changing single-arm phase I/II study of a first-in-class CD123 ADC in an ultrarare aggressive hematologic malignancy where randomized designs are infeasible; high-impact findings appropriate for a top-tier oncology journal with minor revisions.
